children.name: Paracephaelis aristata De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Low-elevation forest; elev. ca 300 m. Flowers: unknown; Fruits: June.

children.name: Paracephaelis bardotiae De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Low-elevation dry, deciduous or semi-deciduous forest; on limestone covered by sand or clay. Flowers: January; Fruits: November.

children.name: Paracephaelis capitulifera De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology High plateau forest, gallery forest; elev. 1200 – 1700 m. Flowers: November – January; Fruits: February – November.

children.name: Paracephaelis cinerea  De Block
children.description: Habitat and phenology Dry deciduous or semi-deciduous forest or forest remnants, dry littoral forest, dry scrub, more rarely subhumid forest; on sandy soil (laterite or white sand) or on rocks; elev. 0 – 1650 m. Flowers: (November –) December – March; Fruits: February – September.

children.name: Paracephaelis comorensis De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Dry forest or thicket, mesophyllous (intermediate) forest; on rocks; elev. 0 – 550 m. Flowers: December – March; Fruits: March – July. According to Barthelat (2019), flowering continues until May, but this was not observed by the author.

children.name: Paracephaelis gautieri De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Low-elevation semi-deciduous forest; elev. ca 300 m. Flowers: January – March; Fruits: unknown.

children.name: Paracephaelis grandifructa De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Mid-elevation humid forest; elev. 500 – 1450 m. Flowers: November – February; Fruits: July – November.

children.name: Paracephaelis longipedicellata De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Littoral, sublittoral or low-elevation humid forest; on sandy soil or rocky substrate; elev. 0 – 450 (– 850) m. Flowers: (January –) March – April; Fruits: March – November. Flower buds were collected in January (3 specs), February (1 spec.) and March (1 spec.). Anthetic flowers were collected in March (flowering peak) and April (2 specs).

children.name: Paracephaelis orientalis De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Littoral or low-elevation humid forest; on sandy soil; elev. 0 – 700 m. Flowers: November (Taolagnaro: McPherson 14410, buds), February (Atsimo-Atsinanana: Tosh et al. 341 B), May (Taolagnaro: Rajoharison et al. 207); Fruits: February – August.

children.name: Paracephaelis pauciflora De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Mid-elevation humid forest; elev. 700 – 1400 m. Flowers: January – March, one collection reported flowering in April (Labat et al. 3079); Fruits: March – December.

children.name: Paracephaelis ranirisonii De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Dry forest; elev. ca 840 m. Flowers: unknown; Fruits: May.

children.name: Paracephaelis russata De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Low-elevation dry deciduous or semi-deciduous forest; on limestone or limestone covered with sand; elev. 40 – 150 m. Flowers: January – March; Fruits: January – July.

children.name: Paracephaelis sambavensis De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Littoral forest; on sand. Flowers: November (flowers buds); Fruits: April.

children.name: Paracephaelis saxatilis  De Block
children.description: Habitat and phenology Deciduous dry forest and scrub, littoral forest and dune vegetation; on white sand, more rarely on rocky substrate; elev. 0 – 1200 m. Flowers: September – October, December – March, May; Fruits: throughout the year, but none recorded in February – March.

children.name: Paracephaelis sericea  De Block
children.description: Habitat and phenology Mid-elevation or lower montane humid forest (500 – 1450 m a. s. l.), rarely low-elevation humid forest (Toliara: Andohahela: 175 – 200 m a. s. l.); on laterite soil. Flowers: October – March, flowering peak in February; Fruits: April – December. The single specimen collected from Toliara (Andohahela) flowers in June.

children.name: Paracephaelis seyrigii De Block, 2022
children.description: Habitat and phenology Deciduous and semi-deciduous dry forest; on sandy soil or rocky substrate; elev. 550 – 1250 m. Flowers: December – January, one collection reported flowering in April (Seyrig 425 B); Fruits: February – May.

children.name: Paracephaelis tiliacea Baill.
children.description: Habitat and phenology Low-elevation dry deciduous forest; on white sand or laterite; elev. 0 – 650 m. Flowers: January – February; Fruits: February – May.

children.name: Paracephaelis trichantha  De Block
children.description: Habitat and phenology Thicket, mixed open and closed scrub; on limestone (outcrops and coral champignons), more rarely on sand; elev. 0 – 650 m. Flowers: November – February (– July); Fruits: February – December. Most specimens flower in January and February. Anthetic flowers were also collected in November (4 specs), March (5 specs), May (3 specs); June (1 spec.), and July (2 specs).

children.name: Hydnophytum acuminicalyx Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mid-level epiphyte in closed forest, 2 000 – 2 400 m; often in large numbers in a single tree. Invariably inhabited by a large form of the aggregate ant species Anonychomyrma scrutator.

children.name: Hydnophytum albertisii Becc.
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Closed or open forest, from 80 – 1 000 m. Tuber contains various arboreal predators including centipedes and spiders, only occasionally with ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum alboviride Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Ridge top, mossy forest, 2 150 – 3 250 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum angustifolium Merr.
children.description: Hydnophytum angustifolium Merr. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Hydnophytum.

children.name: Hydnophytum archboldianum Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Terrestrial or epiphytic in alpine scrub, above 3 000 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum borneanum Becc.
children.description: Hydnophytum borneanum Becc. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Hydnophytum.

children.name: Hydnophytum bracteatum Valeton
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Closed forest, 100 – 1 000 m. Tuber rarely ant-inhabited.

children.name: Hydnophytum buxifolium Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — High-level epiphyte in mossy forest, 2 150 – 2 600 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum caminiferum Wistuba, U.Zimm., Gronem. & Marwinski
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Terrestrial in open scrub and woodland on quartzite soils surrounding the Anggi Lakes in the Arfak Mountains, between 2 000 – 2 600 m. The tuber is once reported with ants, but usually the cavities contain rainwater and various arthropods other than ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum confertifolium Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — High-level epiphyte of mossy forest, 2 150 – 2 600 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum cordifolium Valeton
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, sea level to 300 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum dauloense Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Low to high-level epiphyte in montane forest, 2 400 – 2 800 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants, but collecting rainwater and occupied by a range of invertebrates including cockroaches, centipedes, spiders and on Mt Elimbari the arboreal frog Cophixalus riparius.

children.name: Hydnophytum davisii Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Stunted ridge top Nothofagus forest, at 1 740 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum decipiens Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mossy forest, 1 420 – 2 150 m; on branches of large trees. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum dentrecastense Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — This species is found terrestrially on the upper slopes of Mts Pabinama and Bwebwesu of Normanby Island, at c. 600 – 800 m altitude. This is an area of ultrabasic soils with sparse, stunted forest cover. The tuber is not inhabited by ants and nor does it collect rainwater.

children.name: Hydnophytum ellipticum Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, (? 80 –) 1070 – 1840 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum ferrugineum P.I.Forst.
children.description: Hydnophytum ferrugineum is a epiphyte species of myrmecophytes native to the Cape York Peninsula, Queensland, Australia.

children.name: Hydnophytum formicarum Jack
children.description: Hydnophytum formicarum, commonly called a "Baboon's head" or "Ant plant", is an epiphyte native to Southeast Asia and is considered critically endangered in Singapore.

children.name: Hydnophytum fusiforme Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mossy forest, 2 000 – 2 400 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum grandiflorum Becc.
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Lowland to montane forest, 200 – 1100 m. The tuber appears to be less regularly occupied by ants than H. longiflorum [52], and is often found to be occupied by skinks, geckoes and their eggs, and invertebrates, in particular spiders, myriopods and cockroaches.

children.name: Hydnophytum grandifolium Valeton
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Epiphytic on Casuarina, 160 m. Tuber ant-inhabited.

children.name: Hydnophytum hailans Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, 2 000 – 2 700 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum hellwigii Warb.
children.description: A number of collections from southern Papua New Guinea have broad, elliptic leaves, but in other respects closely match H. hellwigii. Papua New Guinea: Gay 487 (LAE), Western Province, Ok Tedi area, Ok Menga valley. Jacobs 9116 (L), Jacobs 9233 (L), Southern Highlands Province, Waro airstrip, 20 km SSW of Kutubu, S 6 ° 31 ' E 143 ° 10 '. Streimann & Kairo NGF 35950 (A, BRI, BULOLO, CANB, K, L, LAE), Gulf Province, Titamunga, Kukipi subdistrict, S 7 ° 22 ' E 146 ° 03 '. Gray & Floyd NGF 8026 (A,

children.name: Hydnophytum heterophyllum Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — High epiphyte in forest, at 1 200 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum kebarense Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Waterlogged riverine forest, Quercus - Castanopsis forest, 550 – 840 m. Ants not mentioned in collecting notes, but frass in tuber suggests it is ant-inhabited.

children.name: Hydnophytum lauterbachii Valeton
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Unknown, low altitude. Tuber probably ant-inhabited.

children.name: Hydnophytum linearifolium Valeton
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest (?), 200 – 1 500 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum longiflorum A.Gray
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mangroves to montane forest, sea level to 900 m. Usually ant-inhabited, with about 50 % of individual tubers occupied by the ant species Philidris nagasau Mann.

children.name: Hydnophytum lucidulum Valeton
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, 350 – 1 650 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum magnifolium Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, sea level to 600 m. Only once recorded with ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum magnirubrum Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mid- to high-level epiphyte in Nothofagus forest, 2 400 – 2 800 m. Tuber cavities not inhabited by ants, instead occupied by spiders, myriopods and other arthropods.

children.name: Hydnophytum mamberamoense Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — In forest on trees or rockwalls, 100 – 175 m. Apparently not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum mayuense Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, 2 010 m. Occasionally ant-occupied (P. Stevens notes).

children.name: Hydnophytum microphyllum Becc.
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Primary rainforest, sea level to 450 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum minirubrum Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mid- to high-level epiphyte in Nothofagus forest, 2 400 – 2 800 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants, occupied by spiders, myriopods or other arthropods.

children.name: Hydnophytum morotaiense Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, 100 – 800 m. Tuber contents not recorded.

children.name: Hydnophytum moseleyanum Becc.
children.description: {{Speciesbox |name = Smooth ant plant |image = Hydnophytum moseleyanum ALA1.jpg |image_caption = Foliage, flowers and fruit |status = SL |status_system = QLDNCA |status_ref = |taxon = Hydnophytum moseleyanum |authority = Becc.

children.name: Hydnophytum multituberosum Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Epiphytic in open scrub-like forest on ultrabasic soils, 200 – 400 m above sea level. Tuber inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum myrtifolium Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — An epiphyte of mossy forest, from 2 000 – 2 900 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants, but usually containing rainwater, cockroaches, myriopods and sometimes arboreal frogs and their eggs.

children.name: Hydnophytum orichalcum Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Low to mid-level epiphyte in forest, 100 – 500 m. Tuber with or without ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum ovatum Miq.
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, 1 200 – 1 500 m. Tuber inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum pauper Valeton ex Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Terrestrial or epiphytic, 2 550 m. Apparently housing frogs in the cavities, and also once with Paraperipatus (Lam 1945).

children.name: Hydnophytum petiolatum Becc.
children.description: Several collections, which appear to fall into the H. petiolatum complex, are not readily assignable to the above variants, and further collections of this complex may result in alterations to our suggested categories: Collections: NEW BRITAIN, S 5 ° 04 ' E 151 ° 48 ', Mengen Massif, S / D Pomio, Stevens & Lelean in LAE 58790 (A, BRI, CANB, EDIN, K, L). – PAPUA NEW GUINEA, Gulf Province: S 7 ° 30 ' E 144 ° 30 ', Uramu Island, Kikori S / D, Gray & Floyd NGF 8024 (Map 3 m) (A, BRI, K, L). – PAPUA

children.name: Hydnophytum puffii Y.W.Low, Sugau & K.M.Wong
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Epiphytic in swampy forest, waterlogged Agathis forest, lowland to hill kerangas or heath forest over sedimentary rocks and forest over ultramafic geology; 10 – 500 m. Tuber inhabited by ants.

children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, 100 – 1 420 m. Tuber with or without ants.

children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mid to low-level epiphyte in mossy forest, 1 800 – 1 900 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum spathulatum Valeton

children.description: Ecology & Habitat — A low-level epiphyte, regularly becoming terrestrial by falling from tree, becoming buried in leaf litter, and then appearing as a shrub. children.name: Damnacanthus indicus C.F.Gaertn.
children.description:
관목. 높이 4m. 겨울눈 및 소지 정아에 가시가 발달하며, 길이 3-5mm, 달걀형, 끝은 뾰족하고, 아린은 6개이다. 줄기는 마주나기, 혹은 반마주나기이다. 잎자국은 반원형 또는 삼각형이다. 잎 마주나기에서 반마주나기 혹은 짧은 소지에 속생, 잎은 얇고, 좁고 긴달걀형 모양, 크기는 9-15 × 2.5-5.0cm이다. 측맥은 5-6개, 잎 끝은 뾰족하고, 잎 아래는 뾰족하거나 둥글다. 잎 뒷면에 털이 발달하거나 없으며, 약간의 거치가 발달한다. 잎자루는 길이 1-2cm이다. 꽃 암수딴그루, 꽃잎과 꽃받침은 4수이며 수꽃은 10-30개, 암꽃은 2-6개의 꽃이 모여 속생한다. 암꽃에는 수술의 흔적이 있고, 암술대는 2개로 반정도 갈라진다. 꽃받침잎은 삼각형, 꽃잎은 매우 작은 황록색으로 꽃받침열편의 절반 크기이다. 꽃자루는 5-7mm, 털이 있거나 혹은 없다. 열매 및 종자 핵과는 검은색, 열매자루는 5-12mm, 털이 없으며, 종자는 홈이 있다.

개화기 4월말

children.name: Eumachia acuifolia Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in eastern Cuba (LIOGIER, 1963). It has been assumed by various authors that the holotype of Margaritopsis acuifolia is among Wright’s materials at GH, but his specimen numbering is complicated and many of his types need further study.

children.name: Eumachia acutifolia  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Eumachia acutifolia  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr. — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Eumachia.

children.name: Eumachia agustinae  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in eastern Cuba (LIOGIER, 1963).

children.name: Eumachia albert-smithii  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Amazonian Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia and also is disjunct in Suriname (TAYLOR, 2005). DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) reported that this species is “ widespread in South America ”, but it may be restricted to the western Amazon basin. The Suriname plants are only known in immature fruit, and are included in this species provisionally. children.name: Eumachia amoena  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found on Viti Levu and Vanua Levu in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia aneityensis  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to Vanuatu (GUILLAUMIN, 1932).

children.name: Eumachia archboldiana  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found on Viti Levu and Kandavu in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988). The type of this name was originally said to be deposited at “ USNA ” (FOSBERG, 1942; today NA), but was later cited by SMITH & DARWIN (1988) as being at US. Two specimens in the US collection correspond to the original diagnosis and were previously deposited at NA. These sheets are identified as two parts of one collection, and the first sheet is annotated as the type of this name in Fosberg’s writing. Of th

children.name: Eumachia astrellantha  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in the Guianas and Amazonian Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, and northern Brazil (TAYLOR, 2005). See TAYLOR (2005) and DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) for synonymy. DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) reported that this species is found “ throughout Brazil ” but it seems to be restricted to the Amazon basin. Eumachia astrellantha has often been confused with E. chaenotricha, which is found widely in eastern and southeastern Brazil.

children.name: Eumachia balabacensis  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in the Philippines, where it is known from several scattered islands (SOHMER & DAVIS, 2007). It was illustrated by SOHMER & DAVIS (2007: 116, fig. 60). They cited the date of the type collection as January 1913, however the date on the label is August 1913.

children.name: Eumachia boliviana  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: PERU. Coronel Portillo, Chara del Sr Cesar Vela, 25 x 1972, J. Sibunke V. 5461.

children.name: Eumachia carnea  DC.
children.description: Notes. – WHISTLER (1986) reported this species from Fiji, Tonga, and Samoa, and circumscribed it to include Psychotria oncocarpa K. Schum. In contrast SMITH & DARWIN (1988) regarded these as two separate species, and considered Eumachia carnea to be restricted to Tonga; SMITH & DARWIN (1988) are followed here.

children.name: Eumachia cephalantha  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: BRAZIL. Sao Paulo: Piracicaba, estrada para Limeira, 14 vii 1993, V. C. Souza et al. 6001.

children.name: Eumachia chaenotricha  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is commonly collected from eastern Brazil through northern Paraguay (TAYLOR, 2005). See TAYLOR (2005) and DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) for synonymy.

children.name: Eumachia chlorocalyx  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to Upolu in Samoa (WHISTLER, 1986).

children.name: Eumachia coffeosperma  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Cameroon and Democratic Republic of Congo, and its subspecies have separate ranges (VERDCOURT, 1977). The holotype of Psychotria coffeosperma was certainly at the B herbarium and has been destroyed. Several duplicates of the type collection are deposited in other herbaria, and the best sheet, with ample material and both flowers and fruits, is here designated as the lectotype.

children.name: Eumachia collina  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: NEW CALEDONIA. Exploitation forestiere Guiraud piste en direction de Mt Ades (800 – 850 m), sol ferallitique sur peridotites, 25 iii 1988, Jaffre 2951.

children.name: Eumachia cupulicalyx  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Liberia (VERDCOURT, 1977). It was illustrated by VERDCOURT (1977: 800, fig. 3).

children.name: Eumachia cymuligera  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in southeastern Brazil and northern Paraguay (TAYLOR, 2005). TAYLOR (2005) reported the place of deposit of the holotype of Mapouria cymuligera at M, but the specimen at BR with an annotation in Müller’s hand appears to be the actual holotype. Another of M. cymuligera isotype was formerly deposited at B but has been destroyed (photo F neg. # 25701). The identity of M. umbelluligera has not been clear until recently. Its type matches that of M. cymuligera, and in fa

children.name: Eumachia damasiana  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: PAPUA NEW GUINEA. New Britain: north end of Lake Daketana on Willhaumez Peninsula, 30 v 1973, R. S. Isles et al. NGF 32277.

children.name: Eumachia deinocalyx  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Note. – This species was known from the Guianas and eastern through southern Venezuela (TAYLOR, 2005), and has also been recently reported from Amazonian northern Brazil (DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE, 2015; e. g., Farney & Batista 2031, Prance et al. 10647, both at both MO and NY).

children.name: Eumachia depauperata  M.R.V.Barbosa & M.S.Pereira
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in dry vegetation, including caatinga, carrasco, restinga, and semideciduous forest, in Ceará, Paraíba, and Rio de Janeiro in eastern Brazil. Mapouria depauperata was described in an addendum to Müller’s main flora treatment for Brazil, and this name has been overlooked. children.name: Eumachia domatiicola  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Ghana, Nigeria, Cameroon, continental Equatorial Guinea, and Democratic Republic of Congo (VERDCOURT, 1977). RAZAFIMANDIMBISON et al. (2014) cited the type material of Psychotria domatiicola as two specimens deposited at BR, one the holotype and the other an isotype. children.name: Eumachia evansensis  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia extensa  I.M.Turner
children.description: Eumachia extensa  I.M.Turner — a magnoliopsida species in the genus Eumachia.

children.name: Eumachia forsteriana  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species occurs in Fiji, Samoa and Tonga (WHISTLER, 1986; SMITH & DARWIN, 1988). WHISTLER recognized two varieties of this species, but SMITH & DARWIN synonymized them; SMITH & DARWIN are followed here.

children.name: Eumachia frutescens  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.

children.name: Eumachia geminodens  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is endemic to Upolu in Samoa (WHISTLER, 1986). The holotype was deposited at B, where Schumann worked, but has been destroyed.

children.name: Eumachia goodenoughiensis  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Papua New Guinea (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia gossweileri  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the main region of Angola (i. e., not Cabinda; VERDCOURT, 1977).

children.name: Eumachia guianensis  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Guianas (TAYLOR, 2005) and northern to central Brazil (DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE, 2015).

children.name: Eumachia haematocarpa  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found from Nicaragua to northwestern Ecuador (TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia hassleriana  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species was known from Paraguay (TAYLOR, 2005) and has recently also been confirmed from eastern and northeastern Brazil (e. g., Kuhlmann 3958, MO and SP; Stannard et al. H 51938, MO). Four duplicates of the type collection of Rudgea hassleriana are deposited at G, where Chodat worked. The only specimen in his personal herbarium has original drawings and is here considered the holotype.

children.name: Eumachia horsfieldiana  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Java in Indonesia (GOVAERTS et al., 2015). This species has been compared to or confused with Psychotria rostrata Blume. More study will be needed to clarify the identity of the latter.

children.name: Eumachia huallagae  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is known from Amazonian Peru, Bolivia, and western Brazil (TAYLOR, 2005) and has also recently been documented in Ecuador (G. Villa & P. Alvia 982, MO).

children.name: Eumachia impatiens  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found from Nicaragua to northwestern Colombia (TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia inaequifolia  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Bahia and Minas Gerais in eastern Brazil. The identity of Psychotria inaequifolia has been unclear for some time, but it has now been documented by several good collections. These collections show the characteristic flattened ridged internodes, bilobed stipules with glandular lobes and the basal portion becoming hard and yellowed, and red fruits of Eumachia. This species is additionally characterized by its leaves with reticulated higher-order venation that is r

children.name: Eumachia incompta  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found on Viti Levu in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia inconspicua  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Amazonian Venezuela, Brazil, Peru, and Bolivia. Its known range has been extended since its description, and it is not uncommonly collected in Brazil (C. M. Taylor, pers. obs., INPA).

children.name: Eumachia insidens  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Nigeria, Liberia, and Bioko in Equatorial Guinea, and its subspecies have separate ranges (VERDCOURT, 1977). The name Psychotria insidens was based on collections made by Mann in Bioko and deposited at K, which VERDCOURT (1975: 269) detailed as the syntypes Mann 310 and Mann 1155. children.name: Eumachia kappleri  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Guianas, in Amazonian Venezuela, Brazil, and Colombia, and in Costa Rica (TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia lanceifolia  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Haiti (LIOGIER, 1995). The holotype specimen deposited at B, where Urban worked, has been destroyed. Two duplicates of the type collection are deposited in Ekman’s main collection at S, and the sheet with more material on it is here designated as the lectotype.

children.description: PAPUA NEW GUINEA. Madang Province: Ramu Subprovince, Walium Station, 20 iv 1979, Sohmer & Katik LAE 75127.

children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Gabon (VERDCOURT, 1977). A specimen of this species at P is labelled Mann 887, and appears to be an isotype with a typographical error in the collection number (O. Lachenaud, unpubl. data).

children.name: Eumachia lophoclada  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ivory Coast, and Ghana (VERDCOURT, 1977).

children.name: Eumachia lyciiflora  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to New Caledonia (BARRABÉ et al., 2013).

children.name: Eumachia macrocarpa  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Gabon and Democratic Republic of Congo (VERDCOURT, 1977). It was illustrated by VERDCOURT (1977: 795, fig. 2). children.name: Eumachia membranacea  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Note. – This species is found on Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia membranifolia  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species occurs in Papua New Guinea and the Philippines (SOHMER, 1988; SOHMER & DAVIS, 2007). An illustration was presented by SOHMER & DAVIS (2007: 117, fig. 61).

children.name: Eumachia merrilliana  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to the Solomon Islands (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia microdon  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: PANAMA. OIS, 16 vi 1924, L. A. M. Riley SERA 149.

children.name: Eumachia monopedicellata  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Bismarck Archipelago (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia montana  I.M.Turner
children.description: INDONESIA. Sumbawa: 1927, I. Rensch 593.

children.name: Eumachia nana  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Amazonian Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, and Brazil (TAYLOR, 2005; DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE, 2015). See TAYLOR (2005) and DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) for synonymy. The type locality was reported by Ule as Amazonas in Brazil, but the Rio JuruáMirim is actually in today’s Brazilian state of Acre and at the time Ule was there, Acre was still part of Bolivia. The holotype was deposited at B and has been destroyed (photo F neg. # 467).

children.name: Eumachia novohiberiensis  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Bismarck Archipelago (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia nutans  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Cuba and Hispaniola (LIOGIER, 1963, 1995). See TAYLOR (2005) for synonymy.

children.name: Eumachia obanensis  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: CAMEROON. Prov. Sud-Oeust: Dept Fako, Bakingili 50 – 300 m trail to Mt Cameroon, 25 vii 1984, S. A. Thompson & J. E. Rawlins 1662.

children.name: Eumachia obovoidea  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Cameroon and eastern to central Democratic Republic of Congo (VERDCOURT, 1977). Its typical subspecies was illustrated by VERDCOURT (1977: 805, fig. 4). Plants of Eumachia obovoidea are often notable for their corky or thickened stems. Two duplicates of the type specimen of Chazaliella obovoidea are deposited at BR, where the holotype was designated in the protologue without further detail. One of these specimens has a collection label, an annotation with this n

children.name: Eumachia oddonii  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Nigeria, Cameroon, Republic of Congo, and Democratic Republic of Congo. The type material of this name was cited by VERDCOURT (1977: 799) as two collections deposited at BR. One collection, Oddon in Gillet 3746, has not been seen so this name cannot be further typified here. Verdcourt considered Eumachia poggei to be of somewhat unclear identity, but similar to or perhaps not distinct from E. oddonii.

children.name: Eumachia oleoides  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to New Caledonia (BARRABÉ et al., 2013).

children.name: Eumachia oncocarpa  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species occurs in eastern Polynesia, in Fiji and Samoa (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia ovoidea  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in continental southeastern Asia, in Vietnam and Cambodia (GOVAERTS et al., 2015). RUHSAM et al. (2008) concluded that this species does not belong to Chassalia, and transferred it to Psychotria but did not designate a lectotype. This species has the characters of Eumachia rather than Psychotria, and does not match any other Eumachia species treated here. Therefore this name is transferred to Eumachia, but this species is not well understood so but more study will

children.name: Eumachia pallidinervia  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in southern Venezuela (TAYLOR et al., 2004; TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia parviflora  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Note. – This species was known to VERDCOURT (1980) only from the type specimen, from Cabinda in northern Angola.

children.name: Eumachia paupertina  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in southern Venezuela (TAYLOR et al., 2004; TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia podocephala  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Amazonian Colombia, Venezuela, Brazil, and Peru (TAYLOR, 2005). See TAYLOR (2005) and DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) for synonymy. See TAYLOR (2005) also for discussion of the nomenclatural confusion between this species and the unrelated species Psychotria turbinella var. sororiella (Müll. Arg.) Steyerm.
